title: Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
summary: JavaScript is not one program but a family of engines that a defender must treat as separate execution surfaces. On Windows the JScript engine inside Windows Script Host reads .js and .jse files through wscript.exe or cscript.exe, and the same engine backs HTML Application files started by mshta.exe, which bridges script text into Component Object Model objects and the file system. On macOS, JavaScript for Automation is driven by the osascript utility, by compiled applets, or in memory through the OSAKit framework, giving a script the ability to drive applications and reach operating system interfaces. A standalone Node.js runtime executes JavaScript from a terminal, a service, or as a child of another process. The artefact trail is process creation telemetry where the image is a script host and the command line points at a script file, plus the script file itself and any files it drops. The strongest discriminator is lineage and location rather than the interpreter name: a script host spawned by a document reader, a mail client, or a web server, or a script written to a temporary or public directory seconds before it runs, separates abuse from a signed installer or a login script running from a fixed managed path.

beginner.definition: JavaScript is a small programming language that runs inside web pages and also outside them. Many computers already include a program that can read and run JavaScript files. Attackers use those built-in programs to run code of their own. This technique describes that abuse.
beginner.whyItMatters: You cannot simply block JavaScript, because websites and business tools depend on it. The same programs that run it are trusted and already installed on the machine. This means harmful code can run without any new software being installed. If you ignore these programs, you may miss an intrusion completely.
howItWorks: A user opens a file, a link, or a document that holds JavaScript written by an attacker.
A built-in script host, such as the Windows Script Host, starts and reads that file.
The script runs with the rights of the user who started it, not more.
It may download more files, gather information, or talk to a remote server.
On a Mac, the osascript tool is a command line program that runs JavaScript for Automation.
Because the code is plain text, attackers often scramble it to hide what it does.
beginner.example: Imagine a shared office building where every floor has the same vending machine. The machine is useful and nobody thinks about it. One day a stranger learns that the machine also accepts handwritten notes. He writes a note that says open the store room and bring me the boxes. The machine does it, because nothing checks who wrote the note. JavaScript on your computer is like that machine. It is useful, familiar and trusted, so a note from a stranger looks exactly like a note from the staff.
takeaways: JavaScript runs in many places, so blocking one program does not stop it.
Watch which program starts the script runner, not only the script name.
Scrambled script text is a warning sign that deserves a closer look.

objectives: Describe how JavaScript is executed on Windows, on macOS and inside a Node.js runtime.
Explain how this sub-technique differs from the parent technique, Command and Scripting Interpreter.
Identify the process creation events that record a script interpreter starting.
Recognise the parent processes and file paths that make a script run suspicious.
Explain why text-based scripts are often obfuscated and what that looks like in telemetry.
